newsitem.title: USA: SEC freezes profits in Duracell options trade - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: SEC freezes profits in Duracell options trade - WSJ.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission was given permission by a New York court to freeze $950,000 in profits made in trading of options in Duracell International Inc just days before the announcement that the company would merge with Gillette Co, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday.

The trades were made by BSI-Banca de la Svizzera Italiana, a Swiss bank, and Nominees Ltd, a Bahamian holding company, and done through U.S. brokerage firms, the Journal reported, citing information from the SEC.

The Financial Times of London reported in its Tuesday editions that the BSI-Banca de la Svizzera Italiana trades were done through Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, while the Nominees trades were done through Prudential Securities.
The SEC is ordering the parties who placed the trades to identify themselves.
Neither Banca de la Svizzera Italiana, Nominees Ltd or the two U.S. brokerages were immediately available to comment.
